I did not run any experiments or look up benchmark data. These probabilities come from heuristics about NAS-Bench-201, not from measured effects.

- **Replacing "none" with a conv (claim 2):** this gives a large gain, so I rate it likely higher than edits that replace an existing op.
- **Replacing a conv with another conv (claim 29):** this gives little or negative gain, so I rate it unlikely to be higher.
- **Redundant paths:** an edge matters less when another path into the same node is already strong. I rate "add a good op" edits as lower when a parallel edge is already a conv (claims 1, 9, 19, 23).
- **Removing an edge when it is the only strong path:** this hurts more, so claim 22 (edge 3 to none when edge 4 is none) is unlikely to be higher.
- **Everything else:** I could find no strong structural reason either way, so those claims sit at about 20–35.
